newsitem.title: USA: Gateway stock falls on earnings warning rumors.
newsitem.headline: Gateway stock falls on earnings warning rumors.

text.p: Shares of Gateway 2000 Inc. fell in active trading Wednesday even though the direct marketer of personal computers denied rumours -- which sparked the sell-off -- that it will warn of an earnings shortfall Thursday.

The stock fell as low as $57 before ending down $1.375 at $60.75 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the fourth most-active issue on volume of 5.5 million. Trading in its options was also active.
Gateway shares tumbled amid widespread market rumours that the company would pre-announce its second-quarter results at a PaineWebber conference in New York on Thursday.
Shortly before the stock market closed, Gateway denied the speculation. But the response apparently came too late to help the company's stock stage a full recovery.
"We will talk about it (the second quarter) if asked," said a Gateway spokesman. "It's a typical second quarter, which means it's in like a lamb and out like a lion."

One market source said there were also rumours that Gateway had a weak April and May was better, but if June does not pick up, the company will fall short of its second-quarter earnings forecast. The source attributed the weakness to its consumer business.

Gateway, based in North Sioux City, S.D., is expected to release its second-quarter earnings on July 25. The consensus on Wall Street, according to First Call, is for earnings of 90 cents a share for the period, with estimates ranging from 86 cents to 95 cents a share.
Gateway earned $67.5 million, or 86 cents a share, on $1.4 billion in revenues in the first quarter.

The Gateway spokesman said he could not comment any further because the month of June has only just started. He said Gateway officials at the conference will discuss a major initiative to gain more large corporate customers.
Gateway has manufacturing facilities in the United States, Ireland and Malaysia, and has over 10,000 employees worldwide.

The rumours pulled down shares of other personal computers makers as well. Compaq Computer Corp. fell 2-1/8 to 97-7/8 and Dow component International Business Machines Corp. lost one to 83-3/8. Dell Computer Corp. lost 3-3/8 to 104-3/4 in heavy trading.
"It's irrational exuberance turned into irrational panic," said David Wu, an analyst at ABN/Amro Chicago Corp.

Investors remain jittery about personal computer stocks and a slowdown in PC sales, after Intel Corp. stunned Wall Street last Friday by warning that second-quarter earnings will fall short of expectations due to surprisingly weak demand, particularly in Europe.
Seagate Technology Inc. warned late Monday of weaker fourth-quarter results, fuelling concerns among investors about a coming PC slowdown.
